subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: Should OpenClaw add a core web-tool domain egress firewall now, and if so should the accepted contract be a scoped `web_fetch` hostname allowlist, a managed-proxy-owned policy, or a broader cross-tool allow/deny design?
rationale: This adds an operator-trusted security/config surface, and the active related PRs choose different boundaries that automation should not settle without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve Scoped web_fetch Allowlist
options.body: Review and sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step, with deny/search/proxy coverage tracked explicitly as follow-up work.

options.title: Make Managed Proxy the Boundary
options.body: Pause local web_fetch config work and route application-owned egress policy through the managed proxy direction instead.

options.title: Require Cross-Tool Design
options.body: Hold implementation until fetch, search, browser, redirects, caches, provider fallback, plugin HTTP, and deny semantics share one documented policy contract.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped web_fetch Allowlist
recommendation.body: Review and sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step, with deny/search/proxy coverage tracked explicitly as follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history across the SSRF, guarded fetch, and web_fetch runtime surfaces involved in the boundary decision.
